factual_methodological.summary: September payrolls, unemployment, participation, wages and revisions were checked against the 2 October BLS Employment Situation. August PCE inflation and real consumption were checked against BEA; policy rates and projections against the Federal Reserve; 1–2 October yields against U.S. Treasury daily par-yield data.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The brief separates hiring-flow weakness from labour-market level, avoids treating a single payroll print as recession proof, and does not attribute end-of-day Treasury moves mechanically to the employment release.

novelty_against_previous_daily.summary: The lead changes from 2 October's pre-payroll euro-area inflation and Japan labour-demand setup to the now-released U.S. employment data and the employment-inflation-financing-cost trade-off.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 Markdown table + 3 explicit charts + 1 causal flow + 1 regional transmission map per locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: All quantitative visual values are traceable to cited primary releases; EN/PT-BR layouts and values are aligned.

political_neutrality.summary: Federal Reserve trade-offs are described as conditional economic mechanisms without endorsement, opposition, scoring or prediction of a policy decision.

contrary_evidence: The unemployment rate has remained within a narrow 4.1%–4.3% range since March, so the weak September payroll does not establish a broad labour contraction.
Health care, construction and manufacturing still added jobs in September, while participation and the employment-population ratio changed little.
August real PCE rose 0.6%, indicating that household demand remained resilient before the September payroll release.
Treasury yields ended 2 October higher than 1 October across the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year maturities cited, so market pricing did not produce a simple easing signal.
limitations: The Employment Situation combines household and establishment surveys with sampling error and subsequent revisions; one month should not be treated as a structural break.
August PCE predates the September employment report and cannot establish how consumption responded to the latest hiring slowdown.
Daily Treasury yields reflect many factors besides payroll data, including inflation expectations, term premium, issuance, global rates and positioning.
Federal Reserve projections are participant assessments made on information available at the September meeting and are not commitments.
Euro-area and Japan observations are carried forward only as cross-country context; the new evidence in this edition is centered on the U.S. release.
notes: Approved after primary-source verification, bilingual parity review, revision-history check, visual-semantic review and explicit separation of observed yields from causal attribution.

en.title: Global Macro — U.S. payrolls slow to 29,000 as inflation and long yields keep the Fed trade-off asymmetric
en.deck: September payrolls rose only 29,000 and July-August were revised down by 60,000, but PCE inflation remains 3.4% and long Treasury yields stayed above 5%.
en.regime: Slower U.S. hiring under persistent inflation and elevated long yields: labour momentum weakened, but unemployment remains near its recent range and consumption has not yet confirmed a broad contraction.
en.key_risk: If hiring continues to weaken while inflation remains above target and long yields stay elevated, monetary policy can face a sharper employment-inflation trade-off before financing conditions ease.

pt-BR.title: Macro Global — Payroll dos EUA desacelera para 29 mil enquanto inflação e juros longos mantêm o trade-off do Fed assimétrico
pt-BR.deck: O payroll de setembro cresceu apenas 29 mil e julho-agosto foram revisados em -60 mil, mas a inflação PCE segue em 3,4% e os Treasuries longos permaneceram acima de 5%.
pt-BR.regime: Contratação americana mais fraca sob inflação persistente e juros longos elevados: o impulso do trabalho caiu, mas o desemprego segue próximo da faixa recente e o consumo ainda não confirmou contração ampla.
pt-BR.key_risk: Se a contratação continuar enfraquecendo enquanto a inflação permanece acima da meta e os juros longos seguem elevados, a política monetária pode enfrentar um trade-off emprego-inflação mais agudo antes de as condições financeiras aliviarem.
